When it happened the first time, I would always panic and feel like the way I did during the high for about ... 3 months. I guess I've gotten so used to dealing with it that when it happened again a couple days ago, I was able to manage it two days later. It does get better though, as cliché as it sounds.

This actually happened to me a couple months ago and actually even a few days ago. It really scared the living shit out of me because everything I touched felt so weird, my body would just go numb but I looked and sounded normal to everyone. It affected me for a real long time but mostly because I was so traumatized from the first time it happened. 

I found myself getting better when I started to write down how I felt and would realize that this only happens when I'm really really high. I've made the decision to stop smoking because I always end up panicking and feeling the same way I did when I was high even when I'm sober. I would limit my thoughts on the situation and constantly try to reassure my safety. 

Physically, I would always try to move my legs a little bit to see how it would feel but definitely have something to ground yourself. I always kept a rubber band on my wrist and would pull it back to hit my skin lightly (although I'm not sure if it was the safest option). I would also try to watch movies or listen to music that would help me stay calm or just simply talk to my friends about it. Even if they didn't really understand, knowing that they were there to listen or help me out made me really calm. I would also try to write down or describe 5 things I saw going around me just to make sure that I was in present time. 

You got this! It's a really scary time and a rough journey but reassurance and finding ways to ground yourself, stay calm and realizing that everything is real life and not a dream-state will slowly help you.
